Subject: AWS Marketplace deployment patterns and copilot snippet review

Sophie —

Thanks again for the intro earlier this week. We're finalizing the AWS Marketplace listing copy and the example code snippet for the Copilot-style integration. Before we push the listing draft to the seller console, two quick technical/positioning questions from our side: 

1) Deployment pattern: For customers who plan to use our Copilot runtime (server-side calls from their product) do you recommend listing as a container product (ECS/EKS) or AMI-backed listing? We want to make sure the copy aligns with the recommended onboarding path for partners leaning into Copilot and Marketplace procurement.

2) Quantization/instance guidance: we have a short "Recommended infra" section in the draft. Would you prefer we keep it high-level ("GPU-backed instances recommended, see docs") or call out specific instance families for common workloads?

Attached: marketplace_listing_draft_20261118.pdf (draft product page copy), copilot_snippet_v2.txt (example integration snippet), pricing_matrix_20261118.xlsx (placeholder numbers).

Can we get your preferred approach and any required language for the listing (e.g., AMI vs container disclosure) by EOD Tuesday so we can sync with the GTM team? Happy to jump on a 30-min call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace deployment patterns and copilot snippet review

Kimberly —

Thanks — good, pragmatic questions. Quick notes: 

- For Copilot-style integrations where the customer invokes the partner service from their app, container-based listings (ECS/EKS / ECR images) tend to be the clearer path for onboarding and automated provisioning. AMI listings are still fine for ISVs who deliver a pre-configured appliance (on-prem or heavily-customized infra), but they add extra steps to the procurement flow.

- On infra recommendations: keep the public-facing product page high-level ("GPU-backed instances recommended" + a short footnote linking to a technical guide). In the private offer or technical appendix (we can surface one during the seller onboarding) you can be prescriptive — call out instance families and expected memory/throughput for the three common workload profiles. 

- Copy/legal: we require a short sentence if a product is AMI-only or AMI-required. If you don't have an AMI offering, avoid AMI references to reduce confusion in the listing UI.

I'll loop in the approvals queue early (cc'd) so we don't hit surprises in the final submit. Confirming I can review the finalized draft by Mon 23 Nov if you can incorporate the above.

Happy to set a 30-min call Thurs if you want to walk through the draft — shout what works and I can lock time.

Best,
Sophie
Partner Solutions Architect — AWS Marketplace

Sophie — thanks, that's exactly the guidance we needed. We've updated the draft to: 

- Treat container-based listing as primary for the Copilot integration flow, remove AMI-specific language from the public product page.
- Add a private appendix (seller console/LOB-facing) with recommended instance families and perf bands for latency-sensitive vs throughput-heavy workloads.

I've attached a slimmed product page and a tighter copilot snippet that calls out the VPC-association step. Summary of edits below: 

- Hero: emphasize "Predictable inference performance across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments" (keeping claims conservative).
- Technical bullets: call out GPU recommendation + link to appendix (instead of enumerating instance SKUs).
- Copilot snippet: removed AMI boot steps, swapped for container image pull + task definition note.

Next steps: 
- Marissa will run a short copy sweep for GTM tone.
- Jonas to add co-sell enablement bullets for the field (one-pager).

Can you confirm the approvals queue still looks OK for Monday 23 Nov? If so we'll prepare the private appendix and send the final for your review Friday.

Thanks,
Kimberly
